title: Rule 4 deductions explained: what a withdrawn horse takes off your winnings

scenes.say: When a horse is withdrawn after you've bet, the bookmaker can take a Rule 4 deduction from your winnings. Here's how much, and why.
scenes.caption: When a horse is withdrawn after you've bet, the bookmaker can take a Rule 4 deduction from your winnings. Here's how much, and why.

visual.title: What a withdrawn horse takes off your winnings

scenes.say: A late withdrawal gives the rest of the field a better chance, so the odds you took are now bigger than they should be. Rule 4 evens that out with a deduction from the winnings of bets placed before the withdrawal.
scenes.caption: A late withdrawal gives the rest of the field a better chance, so the odds you took are now bigger than they should be. Rule 4 evens that out with a deduction from the winnings of bets placed before the withdrawal.

lines.text: The rest have a better chance
Your price is now too big
A deduction from your winnings evens it out

scenes.say: You bet ten pounds to win at five to one. Then a horse priced at three to one is withdrawn: that's twenty-five pence in the pound. Your fifty pounds of winnings become thirty-seven pounds fifty, so the bet returns forty-seven pounds fifty instead of sixty.
scenes.caption: You bet £10 to win at 5/1. Then a horse priced at 3/1 is withdrawn: that's 25p in the pound. Your £50 of winnings become £37.50, so the bet returns £47.50 instead of £60.

scenes.say: The shorter the withdrawn horse's price, the bigger the deduction. Evens takes forty-five pence. Three to one, twenty-five pence. Six to one, ten pence. Longer than fourteen to one, nothing.
scenes.caption: The shorter the withdrawn horse's price, the bigger the deduction. Evens takes 45p. 3/1, 25p. 6/1, 10p. Longer than 14/1, nothing.

scenes.say: If a six to one runner comes out as well, the deductions add up: thirty-five pence, and the bet returns forty-two pounds fifty. They never go above ninety pence in the pound. And Rule 4 only touches your winnings: your stake comes back in full.
scenes.caption: If a 6/1 runner comes out as well, the deductions add up: 35p, and the bet returns £42.50. They never go above 90p in the pound. And Rule 4 only touches your winnings: your stake comes back in full.

scenes.say: Starting price bets are usually not reduced, unless the horse comes out too late to form a new market. Each-way bets lose the same share on both parts.
scenes.caption: Starting price bets are usually not reduced, unless the horse comes out too late to form a new market. Each-way bets lose the same share on both parts.

items.text: Starting price bets: usually no deduction
Unless the runner comes out too late for a new market
Each way: the same share off both parts
